scope.summary: This standard specifies standard guidelines, limiting and optimum environmental thresholds, operational control criteria, and regulatory parameters for controlling attacks by vertebrate and invertebrate pests on stored cereals and pulses in India.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Code of Practice / Design and Operational Guidelines (Food and Agriculture / Post-Harvest Management)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 11816 (Part 3) is an operational guideline and code of practice for pest control rather than a physical consumer product, it does not carry a mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, compliance with its pest exclusion rules, insect multiplication curves, and FSSAI pesticide residue limits is strictly mandated in public sector grain storage and procurement tenders (issued by the Food Corporation of India (FCI), Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC), and state warehousing agencies) across India to safeguard national buffer stocks. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.

requirements.detail: Recognizes that the ability of birds, rats, mice, and other rodents to feed on grain is not limited by the quality or condition of the grain but only by its physical accessibility, mandating structural exclusion measures.

Pest control regulations and chemical applications must strictly take into account and comply with the recommendations of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) regarding limits for pesticide residues in food.

Requires implementing specific controls to manage pre-harvest field infestations caused by storage insects (primarily Sitotroga cerealella and Sitophilus zea-mais) flying from warehouses to lay eggs on ripening crops, which particularly impacts hybrid maize with short sheath leaves.

requirements.requirement_type: Pest Temperature and Humidity Boundaries (Appendix A)

requirements.detail: Any observed or calculated test or analysis value expressing moisture content, temperature, humidity, or pest counts must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained must be identical to the specified value in the standard.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 11816 (Part 3) : 2018 (First Revision) is the national Indian Standard guidelines specifying criteria for controlling pest attacks on stored cereals and pulses. Developed by the FAD 16 Sectional Committee, this standard integrates structural exclusion, chemical safety, and biological temperature/humidity thresholds to protect stored grain. It mandates structural barriers to exclude rodents and birds (whose feeding is limited only by accessibility), requires compliance with FSSAI pesticide residue limits, and outlines precise environmental limits that control the multiplication of destructive insect pests (such as the rice weevil and lesser grain borer) to guide warehouse aeration and sanitation.
